Ashok Towers Marol CHS Ltd., Krishanlal Marwah Marg, Off Military Road, Marol, Andheri East, Mumbai - 400072.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Malad Fish Market is a great place to buy fresh fish at good prices. You can get discounted rates if you buy in bulk, and bargaining skills definitely help here. There’s a wide variety of fresh seafood available, and the quality is good if you choose carefully.
The market can be crowded and busy, but that’s part of the experience. Best place for people who know how to negotiate and want value for money.

featured_reviews.name: ViSHAL SUTAR
featured_reviews.review_text:
1.	Freshness & Variety
•	Wide range of sea fish and also crabs.  ￼
•	Fish catches are fresh; many comment that it’s among the best places for seafood lovers.  ￼
2.	Value for money / Wholesale rates
•	Prices often more reasonable than smaller local shops, especially if you buy early or in bulk.  ￼
•	Ability to bargain.  ￼
3.	Additional services
•	Fish cleaning / cutting service available. Some vendors provide cleaning without extra cost or for a small charge.  ￼
•	Open long hours—starting early in morning through most of the day.  ￼
4.	Location & accessibility
•	Near Malad Railway Station, so relatively easy for many people to reach.  ￼
5.	Atmosphere
•	“Vibe” of a genuine fish market: lively, bustling; people like the authenticity.

featured_reviews.name: bashir shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
That's wonderful to hear! The Malad Fish Market in Mumbai is indeed very well-known for being a bustling, vibrant hub.
​It's famous for:
​Wholesale and Retail: It's a major market where you can buy a vast variety of fresh saltwater fish at both wholesale and retail prices.
​Variety of Seafood: You can find everything from prawns, pomfret, Bombay duck, and crabs, often straight from the catch.
​Location: It's conveniently located on Sainath Road, very close to the Malad West railway station.
​It sounds like you had a great visit! What did you find particularly amazing about it?

featured_reviews.review_text: It was crowded but not heavily. Ideal timings are 6 to 7 am in the morning you will get fresh catch there. Bargaining doesn't work for me but if you have good bargaining skills you can buy at affordable price.

featured_reviews.name: Sushil Malik
featured_reviews.review_text: Malad Fish Market is a large, busy seafood market in Malad West, just a short walk from Malad railway station (West) on Sainath Road, and is popular for fresh, relatively low-priced sea fish. Location and access Located on Sainath Road, very close to Malad Railway Station (West); it is  2–5 minutes from the station. Timings  roughly 6:00 am onwards; morning hours are the main time when the wholesale and freshest stock comes.Locals recommend going around 6:00–7:30 am if you want the best catch and prices, especially if buying in bulk. Market layout and what you getThe market is divided into multiple sections: unloading/wholesale area on the road, a covered retail area where they also clean and cut, and open sections where you buy and then pay extra at cutting counters. You typically get a wide variety of saltwater fish like pomfret, surmai, bangda, bombil, prawns, crabs and seasonal catch, with both retail and wholesale options. Tips for visiting Go early, carry change, and be ready to bargain hard; prices are better if you buy in larger quantities.It is a traditional wet market, so expect crowds, strong smell, and wet floors. simple washable footwear and carrying your own bags can be more comfortable.If you tell what exactly you want (pomfret, prawns, bulk/retail, specific budget),

featured_reviews.review_text:
Serving the finest cakes at not too exorbitant price

Have tried cakes, pastries, puffs, and many other foodstuffs from merwans, but each time I try these guys become better and better. This time I had tried the half kg version of the strawberry ganache flavor and it was absolutely delicious.

The cake has three layers of cream with soft chocolate flavored bread as the base. The topmost layer on the cake is pure white cream and it does taste delicious. It has a small dollop of strawberry jam at the top and nice design of chocolate cream on one side over the white cream. the second layer is the strawberry cream mixed with vanilla as I tasted. you can feel the sweet strawberry taste mixed with vanilla and you can see the light pinkish color of the cream.

The third layer has pure chocolate cream and you either eat all the three one at a time or at once each way you get a unique taste and that taste of the cream melting in your mouth. All in all, this was a wonderful flavor and truly loved the taste of the cake.

featured_reviews.name: Preity M
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vakola and Kalina market is a complete supermarket in itself. Be it household items , grocery, toys, veggies, fruits, daily essentials, Pooja things , you name anything and it's available there. Even all types of restaurants be it vegetarian or non vegetarian or sea food delicacies or  bakery products or designer cakes....everything available at your doorstep and too fresh. People are full of energy and smiling always. I explored this place on foot and found army area too in this area that makes it one of the safest places to live in Mumbai. There is a mixture of independent houses/bungalows, apartments,  low rise complexes, high rise apartments, big shops, small shops, vendors, handcart and the list goes on and on. There is Kalina university nearby this area. The best part is you can catch trains fir Central, Harbour or Western lines from Santacruz Station, Sion Station or Kurla Station which are approx.at equidistant. What more can you want in Mumbai....

There is a different level of energy everywhere in Mumbai. Both these markets are in Santacruz east and at walkable distance from western express highway. I love Amchi Mumbai, its style, aroma, liveliness, glamor, aura and ❤❤❤❤❤💝💝💝💝💝💖💖💖💖💖💓💓💓💓💗💗💗💗💗💗💗💗🙃

featured_reviews.name: Surendra Yadav
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you want to eat authenticate North East food of Manipur, Nagaland this is a place which can serve it. We ordered only North East dishes (strictly No Chinese) . We ordered

Soups
Veg Thukpa soup
Spicy Crab meat soup

Starters
Kungpao Potatoes-patatoes sauted withtm tomato sauce. The taste is sweet and pungy.

Sinju -kind of bhel made of cabbage, dry shrimps, nut powder, pepper spice. Try once somethng different.

Pork Chilli - Taste is good and must try dish.

Main course
Smoke Hoksa (Pork) Gravy With Bamboo Shoot .
Shoot/Yam/Aloo/Naga Dal/Garden Egg
in combination with
Thotrin steam sticky rice.

All dishes tasted different since never ate northeast foodbutv were tasty and delicious.

Ambience The cafe is limited seat enclosure with kitchen ground floor and seating on the upperdeck. The place is purely if someone wants to eat authentic North East food otherwise not a typical restaurant or place to hang out.

Parking available on the street. No private parking available.

The Chefiand other staff all are humble and ready to guide you to order.

Service: Almost all the dishes we ordered came within 10-15mins.

No alcohol served,. Cold drinks are available.

Cleanliness: Cannot compare it with a restaurant or a cafe like Macd but adequately maintained. Cutlery were proper restaurant style.

review_photos.caption: Smoked Hoksa with Bamboo shoot gravy (must try)

featured_reviews.name: Veikho Asanii
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the pioneer North East restaurants in Mumbai.
Thotrin Cafe, located in the heart of Kalina, serves authentic Northeast dishes. The restaurant has two floors of seating and offers a wide variety of food. I’ve tried almost their entire menu — from Kangshoi to noodles, Thotrin Special to pot rice — and everything has been excellent.

It’s also a great place and only NE outlet for bulk orders. Special thanks to Amei Yaomi for his kind-hearted service towards customers. Highly recommended — you will never regret it. They truly feed you well!

featured_reviews.name: Yoh
featured_reviews.review_text:
This Manipuri restaurant has been around for a while now and is serving some delicious soul food. I have been to restaurant and also ordered from there a few times.

Started off with the Seisa salad which is crunchy and pungent; not for the faint hearted. The Smoked Hoksa with Aloo and Bamboo shoot is my favourite currently, paired with their Thotrin rice. The innards masala curry was also delicious. I ask for the Ngari (fermented dry fish with King chilli) which is a flavour bomb. I tried the chicken salad which was not as impressive.

I’m looking forward to trying more of their meals and I’m sure each one will be authentic and its own way.

featured_reviews.name: Beni Ngullie
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Famous North East restaurant in Mumbai, which serves homely made food !!
Loved it.. i think this is the fourth or fifth time i have been there and i am still amazed on how they win me over everytime!!!

Go for it !! The price and the food !! Just so good !!

Please do try the fermented banana wine !!

You will love every bit of it!!

featured_reviews.name: geethu k gopi
featured_reviews.review_text: I would love to give them 5 star but honestly, the atmosphere was very uncomfortable. The food was great.. the space is small was also okay, but the smell from the meat shop near it was so uncomfortable and so strong of dead chickens that It made me nauseous..i couldn’t enjoy eating momos for it packed and ate it at home. The staff is so sweet and nice…a small suggestion for the owners..your food is great. May be you should move to another space and let everyone enjoy the food breathing good air..

featured_reviews.name: Sam Jerry
featured_reviews.review_text: The food was excellent. We ordered thukpa soup and crispy chicken rice it was so delicious tangy flavour. The soup was tempting. The staff lady was also very sweet and dedicated. The place was cozy

featured_reviews.name: Apollo Eliazer
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you want to eat NAGA Cuisine, Tangkhul Cuisine this is the perfect spot to eat.
Ask the staff about the food to understand what's the content of each dish, also for recommendations.
Ask for the level of spice before ordering if you're having low spice tolerance.

Over-all it is an experience. If you don't have northeastern friends to cook for you or have never visited the northeast - this is definitely going to be a great experience and a good investment.

Come here only focusing on food, if you care too much about ambience, don't come here. Cleanliness is maintained and there is a clean washroom too.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve had Naturals Ice Cream before, but this was my first time visiting their parlour — and I loved it! The place is small but has a really cool interior and is super clean and hygienic.

Now coming to the ice cream — oh my goodness! The coconut flavour is hands down my favourite and an absolute must-try. True to its name, the ice creams here are made with natural ingredients, and every flavour tastes rich and authentic. They also offer a variety of fruity options to choose from.

If you haven’t visited this place yet, you’re definitely missing out. Go treat yourself!

featured_reviews.name: Hitesh Harisinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tucked away in a tiny lane in Vakola, this cozy restaurant has barely 6–7 tables, giving it an intimate, no-frills charm. What truly stands out is the hospitality — the staff makes you feel like you're being fed at someone’s home, and that love reflects in the food.

Their traditional meal/thali is served on a banana leaf and is pure comfort. It includes 4 vegetables, 4 varieties of curries, pickle, chutney, and unlimited rice — wholesome, hearty, and incredibly satisfying.

Also, tried -

Surmai Pollichatu – Absolutely the BEST! Perfectly cooked, bursting with flavor, and paired beautifully with soft appams. A must-order.

Buff Fry – Delicious, flavorful, and a perfect companion to parottas.

Prawns Fry – Took a bit long to arrive and was just okay compared to the other standout dishes.

The best part? Four of us ate to our heart’s content for just ₹830! They even served papad and a small cup of payasam on the house. Incredible value for money.

Great food, warm service, generous portions, and prices that make you want to come back again — honestly, what more could you for..

featured_reviews.name: Bhavya Bhat
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Kalavara Kitchen on a Sunday thinking it would be packed, but luckily got a table right away. It’s a small, quaint place with a warm vibe, and the staff were super friendly and welcoming. We tried the Kerala Meal (3.5/5),Chicken Kizhi Biryani (3.5/5), and Payasam (5/5) Portions were decent for the price. Overall, a cozy spot worth visiting once in a while!

featured_reviews.name: Vidya Bhat
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had ordered their Potichor, which is like a wholesome Kerala-style meal packed in a banana leaf.

I had ordered three types — veg, chicken, and egg.

The quantity is really generous for the price, one Potichor is easily enough for two people, especially if you’re someone who doesn’t eat too much rice. A small suggestion to make the experience would be to give some more Sambhar as the rice gets a bit dry. Also, adding a pappadam on the side would make the meal absolutely perfect!

Overall a good dish to explore Kerala style meal 👍🏻

PS. The content of Potichor is Rice, Beans Sabji, Raw Banana Chana Sabji, Pickle, Coconut Based Chutney, Protein of your choice(Omelette or Chicken Fry pieces), Sambhar, Aviyal and curd based curry.

featured_reviews.name: REENA SAM
featured_reviews.review_text: If you’re craving authentic Kerala food in Mumbai, this place is a real lifesaver! The meals taste homely with the right Kerala flavors-spice done perfectly. Fish curry, appam, meals and beef fry are must-tries. Prices are reasonable, portions are good, and service is friendly. The place is simple and not fancy, but the food makes up for it.

featured_reviews.name: Denise
featured_reviews.review_text: Quick service and tasty kerala cuisine. Feels like home cooked food. 10/10

featured_reviews.name: Aasavari Sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
No frills, pocket friendly, good Kerala style food but a bit spicy for our taste.

Busy place in a quiet lane in Kalina. We ordered Kalavara special platter which was enough for 3 people (picture enclosed). Although there were enough options of breads in it, the quantity of curries and dry dishes were not enough to compliment the breads; we had to order an additional portion of curry. Having said that, everything served in the platter was packed with flavour and spice!

featured_reviews.name: K. “ContentName” F.
featured_reviews.review_text:
The entrance was quite busy, with many people standing and chatting — it seems to be a popular evening hangout spot. Inside, the seating is simple and no-frills, with wooden tables and benches. There's a wash basin available.

The staff were friendly. However, not all seemed well-informed about the menu items, which could be a bit of a drawback if you're looking for recommendations or ingredient details.

I ordered Rajavinte Chattichoru and Malabar Chicken Korma , both of which had strong, authentic Kerala flavors. That said, I found both dishes a bit too spicy for my personal taste.

A concern I had was related to how the cleaning mop was stored alongside banana leaves. Something they need to change.

Overall, this place is great for solo meals or hanging out with friends. I wouldn’t recommend it for a date. I will certainly visit again to try the other dishes. Yet to find my favorite.

Rajavinte Chattichoru - 3/5 (Multiple dishes in a bowl instead of a bannana leaf. Quantity sufficient for 3 people. The taste of tamrind was too strong)
Malabar Chicken Kurma - 4/5 (Delicious, but spicy)

The shop was clean, and the ordering process was smooth, both in-store and online. However, adding a few more details about the sourcing of the fish on the website would be a great touch. Overall, highly recommend this shop for anyone looking for quality dry fish!
